content.content:
## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"E1 — the range the model stated, labelled as stated, and *not yet* an ensemble"**, because it is the only option that keeps one meaning in one field, keeps the word *agreement* honest, spends nothing it cannot yet show a return on, and leaves the door open in the one place where the return could actually be measured.

### What ships

A model belief's likelihood and its two range ends are **what the proposal stated**. Nothing rewrites them and nothing widens them. The label does not change either: record 0014's chip already reads *model interval, uncalibrated · how sure we are of `.35` — not how much the world can move*, and the two chip sentences settled on 2026-09-17 — one for a number a world has worked through the map, one for a number that has only been stated — already cover both cases (`spec/workbench/tiles-ports-wires.md`). There is **nothing new on screen, nothing new in code, and nothing extra in a recording**.

### Why not an ensemble now — four reasons anyone can check

1. **It would put a second meaning in a field that already has one.** Record 0014 defines `lo` and `hi` as the 10th and 90th percentiles of the likelihood itself — *if we somehow learned the true likelihoods, about eight times in ten the answer would land in here*. The spread of several answers to the same question measures a different thing: how much one model wobbles when asked twice. Both are interesting. They are not the same quantity, and one field must not carry two meanings.
2. **Re-asks are not independent runs, so calling their spread *agreement* would over-claim.** Every call in this pipeline shares one cached system prompt and one map-so-far (record 0006). Answers drawn from the same prompt and the same partial map are correlated by construction. `spec/vocabulary.md` reserves *agreement* for a number computed from things that were worked out independently; a measurement taken this way would not be one.
3. **It multiplies the bill and makes the reader wait.** Two further generations of a thirty-claim map is about eighty more calls, at record 0006's estimate of about forty calls per map; asking three times for each of thirty claims is ninety asks. The 2026-09-17 design review put the cost of an ensemble at **four to five times the stack's model spend — an estimate made in that review, not a measurement**. And a claim cannot be accepted onto the map until its numbers are settled, so every extra ask slows the map's own growth by that much — the opposite of what FR-5 and UX-8 ask for, which is a map that grows as fast as the model can propose.
4. **A "trimmed mean" of three answers is just the middle one.** Trim the highest and the lowest of three and one number is left. The phrase makes a median sound like a statistical procedure. If this is ever measured, the word to use is **median**.

### Never reconcile whole maps

Option E4 is refused outright, and not only for this stack. The warrant is one level up, in `spec/multiverse/diff.md` anti-pattern 4, quoted as it stands there:

> **4. Do not infer a difference by matching two maps.** *Because* a difference reconstructed after the fact cannot tell "the user supposed this" from "the model happened to number it differently this run", cannot recover the order the edits were made in, and turns a free, exact answer into a guess — the same reason `branches-and-worlds.md` refuses to derive a branch by diffing two maps. **Do** build both worlds from one base map, one seed and two branches, and read the difference off the two results.

Matching one generated map against another is that anti-pattern with nothing held fixed at all: not the base map, not the claims, not their wording, not their identifiers. Whatever such a comparison reported, no one could say how much of it was the world and how much was the model numbering things differently this run. **FR-8 is amended in the same pull request as this record** to say what ships instead, and the standing open question in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §13 moves to the answered list with a sentence saying **the question changed** — not that it was answered.

### The known cost of this decision, said plainly

**Stated ranges run narrow.** Record 0014 records the evidence under its *More Information*, as input to this decision: **FermiEval (2025) — a nominal 90 per cent range covered the truth 28 per cent of the time**; QuantSightBench (2026) reproduced it; Paleka and colleagues (ICLR 2025) found stated ranges incoherent under rewording. Quote that figure with that source wherever it is repeated.

So the ranges this decision ships are, on published evidence, too narrow, and nothing here fixes that. What the product does instead is refuse to pretend otherwise: the chip says **uncalibrated**, in those words, for exactly this reason, and the Inspector says in a full sentence that nobody has checked whether the eight-in-ten holds up, because no claim on any map has resolved yet. A narrow range that says it is unchecked is honest. A wider range manufactured from three correlated answers, wearing the word *agreement*, would not be.

### What would reopen this

One route, and it runs through a measurement rather than through an argument:

1. **The eval scorecard is the baseline.** `spec/generation/evaluation.md` names the scorecard's fields in this same stack, so a later change has something to be compared against rather than being compared against a memory.
2. **The pastcast is the test.** FR-30 runs a chain on an event that has already resolved, with a date-frozen corpus, and reports the standard accuracy score for probability forecasts *including when it is bad*. That is the first moment this repository can see whether a stated range actually misses.
3. **If it misses badly, measure whether re-asking helps** — whether the **median** of several answers is a better point, and whether their spread widens the range *toward the truth* rather than merely widening it. Then decide, with numbers.

Until that day the word **agreement** stays free on screen: the delta rail's column is headed *same direction*, and the field behind it stays `agreement`, so nothing has to be renamed if a run-to-run number is ever earned.

### What it means for the code

* **No `engine/ensemble.py`**, and no code path that asks for a claim's numbers more than once.
* **No new field** on a belief, a link, a proposal or a world. In particular there is no `agreement` anywhere but the diff, and no second range beside the stated one.
* **Nothing extra in a recording.** A recording carries one answer per claim, so a replayed map is the map a live run would have drawn.
* **Nothing new on screen.** No card, no badge and no sentence saying *runs agree*.

### Consequences

* Good, because the number on a chip is the number the model gave, and the label says so — one hop from the screen to the source, which is what the traceability veto asks for.
* Good, because `lo` and `hi` keep exactly the meaning record 0014 gave them, so the two-loop engine, the width shares and the diff all keep reading the same quantity.
* Good, because the word *agreement* keeps one definition, and the day a run-to-run number is earned it can take the word without anything having to be renamed or explained away.
* Good, because the stack's money goes to building the pipeline, the stream, replay and the evals rather than to four or five times the calls for an improvement nobody can yet measure.
* Bad, because the ranges on a fresh map are, on published evidence, too narrow — FermiEval's nominal 90 per cent covering 28 per cent of outcomes — and this decision ships them anyway, mitigated only by saying *uncalibrated* out loud.
* Bad, because FR-8 as originally written is not built in version 1, and a reader who knew the old wording must be told the question changed; §13 says so rather than quietly dropping it.
* Neutral, because nothing here is hard to revisit: adding a second ask later touches the pipeline and one chapter, and adds no field to the domain.

### Confirmation

* `test_the_word_agreement_means_same_direction_and_nothing_else` — a test that reads our own source, in the manner of the existing `test_beliefs_never_merged`: the only `agreement` in `backend/` is the diff's same-direction share.
* `grep -rn "ensemble" backend/src` finds nothing.
* Review item: a proposal is asked for once per claim; no recording under `backend/recordings/` carries two answers for one claim.
* Review item: no screen and no prompt contains the words *runs agree*.
* `spec/generation/evaluation.md` names the scorecard's fields, so the baseline this decision would be reopened against exists before anything is compared to it.

+A contract somebody already sells, or a move in the price of something traded.
+Which one an answer is, is read off `kind` and nothing else.

    tidying ever changes, every recording made before it can be told from every
    recording made after, which is exactly what this is for.

    It deliberately does **not** cover the varying half. That differs on every
    call by design, and folding it in would make the fingerprint useless.

class FoundPage(BaseModel):
    """One page the search tool itself returned during a call.

    Not a page the model mentioned, and not a page anybody went looking for after
    the fact: one the tool handed back, in the order it handed it back. The
    difference is the whole of how an arrow earns the word `documented`.

    It carries no day. The day is a fact about the run rather than about the page,
    so it is stamped on in `grounding.py` where a source is built.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    url: str = Field(description="Where the page is. One address that opens.")
    title: str = Field(description="What a reader sees on arriving, in the publisher's words.")


class Said(BaseModel):
    """One question's answer, translated out of the library's types into ours.

    Three fields carry what happened and six carry what it cost. They are kept
    apart on purpose: **what the model wrote and what the search returned arrive
    in two different fields**, so no code downstream could mistake one for the
    other, which is the mistake the whole grounding rule exists to prevent.

    `calls` counts round trips rather than questions. A question whose answer came
    back part finished is sent straight back to be continued, and each trip is on
    the bill.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    answered: Proposal | StartingClaim | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "What the model answered with, already checked against the shape the "
            "call asked for. Nothing at all when it declined, or when it wrote "
            "nothing we could read."
        ),
    )
    found: tuple[FoundPage, ...] = Field(
        default=(),
        description=(
            "What the search tool returned during this call, in the order it "
            "returned it. Never anything the model typed."
        ),
    )
    declined: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "One plain sentence, when the vendor's own safety check turned the "
            "call down. Nothing at all otherwise. A refusal is shown to the "
            "person, never hidden and never quietly re-routed."
        ),
    )
    calls: int = Field(default=1, description="How many round trips this question took.")
    searches: int = Field(default=0, description="How many web searches it ran.")
    input_tokens: int = Field(default=0, description="Tokens of question read fresh.")
    output_tokens: int = Field(default=0, description="Tokens of answer written.")
    cache_read_tokens: int = Field(default=0, description="Tokens recognised from an earlier call.")
    cache_write_tokens: int = Field(default=0, description="Tokens written into the cache.")
    thinking_tokens: int = Field(
        default=0,
        description=(
            "How many of those written tokens were the model thinking rather than "
            "answering. Half to two-thirds of a call, measured on the first recorded "
            "five, and never shown — so this is the only way to find out where a "
            "minute went without running the whole thing again."
        ),
    )
    seconds: float = Field(
        default=0.0,
        description=(
            "How long this question took, wall clock, measured at the seam. The other "
            "half of the same measurement: tokens say what was written, this says how "
            "long the writing took."
        ),
    )


# --- What our own code decided ----------------------------------------------


class Accepted(BaseModel):
    """A proposal that passed every rule, with the identifiers we minted for it."""

| `engine/receipt.py` | 224 | Running total: `fold`, `dollars_for`, `over_the_cap`. |
| `engine/following.py` | 195 | **Not** the walk driver — an adapter that folds each outcome into transcript + receipt, then yields its event. |

All are `BaseModel` with `model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)`.

### `Ranged` — proposal.py:58
```python

    @model_validator(mode="after")
```

Bounds: `[0,1]` each, plus `lo <= p <= hi`. **This is the only numeric validator in the whole proposal file.**

### `SourceDraft` — proposal.py:116
Exactly one field:
```python
    url: str = Field(description=("One address that opens, not a search query, and one the search tool returned to you in this call rather than one you are recalling."))
```
No title, no date, no quote, no locator — deliberate: "The day it was fetched is the day *our* retrieval step fetched something, and the title is what the search tool itself reported" (proposal.py:123-127).

### `LinkDraft` — proposal.py:139 (this is the "EdgeProposal"; no type of that name exists)
```python
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"] = Field(...)
    strength: float = Field(description=("How far this arrow shifts the effect's odds while the push is at full size, on the scale where separate pushes add up instead of multiplying. Signed: positive makes the effect more likely to be true, negative less likely. Roughly: +1 triples the odds, -1 cuts them to a third. This is not a probability."))
    lag: int = Field(description=("Whole days from the cause becoming true to the push reaching full size. 0 means the same day."))
    shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"] = Field(...)
```

**Answer: yes — `cause` is a single `str` (proposal.py:293-299).** One claim, one parent, one arrow. There is no list, no multi-parent slot, no conjunction/inhibitor field anywhere in the file.

### `LinkProposal` — proposal.py:303 — **yes, it exists**
```python

    source: str = Field(description="The cause: one of the short names this call's map listed.")
```

### Union / envelope
```python
Proposal = Annotated[ClaimProposal | LinkProposal | Stop, Field(discriminator="kind")]   # proposal.py:341
```
The **envelope** is `OneProposal` in `engine/client.py:155`:

It exists only because the service rejects a top-level `anyOf` with `$defs` (client.py:158-165). Put on at `Model.proposal` (client.py:437), taken off at `what_it_said` (client.py:541-543). `StartingClaim` is sent bare (no envelope).

`claim: str`, `resolution: Resolution`, `prior: Ranged`, `base_rate: BaseRate | None = None`. No `kind`, no `cause`, no `link`.

## 3. The walk driver

**It is `grow.py`, not `following.py`.** `following.py` never decides anything — its contract is "Never decide anything about a map, and never call a model. It reads a walk" (following.py:16). Its loop is:

```python
# following.py:87-98
        try:
            for step in walking:
                if isinstance(step, Finished):
                    self.finished = step
                    break
                self._fold(step)
                if not makes_an_event(step):
                    continue
                yield growth_event(step, self.at - 1)
        except Exception:
            logging.getLogger(__name__).exception(...)
            self.broke = WENT_WRONG
```

### The real loop — `grow()` at `engine/grow.py:124`
1. `start_the_map(hypothesis, is_the_hypothesis=True, ...)` via `_keep_asking` (up to `caps.refusals_in_a_row` = 3 attempts, none told why the last failed) — grow.py:175-201.
2. Optional second `start_the_map(target, is_the_hypothesis=False, ...)` — grow.py:213-230. **The destination never joins the frontier** (comment at grow.py:227-228).
3. The round loop — grow.py:232-274:
```python
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=caps.at_once) as pool:
        while not walk.stopped and walk.frontier:
            if len(graph.propositions) >= caps.claims:
                walk.the_map_is_full()
                break
            room = caps.claims - len(graph.propositions)
            asking = list(walk.frontier[: min(caps.at_once, room)])
            walk.watch(answerer)
            answers = _ask_about_each(pool, graph, asking, target=target, answerer=answerer, on=on,
                                      searches_left=caps.searches - walk.receipt.searches)
            walk.bill(answers)
            waiting = list(zip(asking, answers, strict=True))
            while waiting:
                claim_id, answer = waiting.pop(0)
                graph, outcome = walk.fold(graph, claim_id, answer)
                try:
                    yield outcome.model_copy(update={"frontier": tuple(walk.frontier)})
                except GeneratorExit:
                    ...
```
4. Last ending-only pass — grow.py:279-294: `expand(..., ending_only=True)` per line in `_lines_with_no_ending`, folded with `growing=False`.
5. One `Finished` with `_why_it_stopped` (grow.py:809-832): `spend_cap` > `no_terminal` > whatever closed the last open claim (`claim_cap`/`depth_cap`/`width_cap`/`refusal_cap`) > `reached_terminal`.

### Next-step decision
Frontier is a plain FIFO list. `open_a_line` appends (grow.py:374-377); an accepted claim joins it only if non-terminal:
```python
# grow.py:441-450
            arrived = result.proposition
            if growing and arrived is not None and arrived.kind not in TERMINAL_KINDS:
                self.open_a_line(arrived.id, layer=self.layer[claim_id] + 1)
            if growing:
                self._close_if_out_of_room(graph, claim_id)
                if arrived is not None and arrived.id in self.frontier:
                    self._close_if_out_of_room(graph, arrived.id)
```
Lines close on: `Stopped` (grow.py:420-422, reason `"ended"`), 3 refusals in a row (grow.py:430-434), depth cap, width cap (grow.py:501-516), or `the_map_is_full`.

### Does it ever request a `LinkProposal` / cross-link?

**During the walk: it never *asks* for one specifically, but it will accept one, because every expand call sends the `OneProposal` union.** The only thing that mentions cross-links to the model is the standing text (prompt.py:136-141):
```
What an answer is.
Exactly one of three things:
  a new claim, together with the one arrow that reaches it from a claim already
  on the map;
  an arrow between two claims that are both already on the map;
  or a note that this part of the story is finished, with one sentence saying
  why.
```
`expanding_question` (prompt.py:362-443) never narrows to or toward a link; when the claim is near the start with no step yet it actually pushes the *other* way via `ASK_FOR_A_STEP_FIRST` (prompt.py:436-437, 446-455).

**The dispatch** — `expand.py:122-132`:
```python
    if said.declined is not None:
        return costing(Refused(claim_in_words=said.declined), frontier, said)

    proposed = said.answered
    if proposed is None or isinstance(proposed, StartingClaim):
        return costing(
            Refused(claim_in_words="The model gave no answer to this question."), frontier, said
        )
    if isinstance(proposed, Stop):
        return costing(Stopped(why=proposed.why), frontier, said)
    return costing(_judge(graph, proposed, found_in(said, on=on)), frontier, said)
```
i.e. anything that is a `ClaimProposal` **or** a `LinkProposal` falls through to `_judge`. The link branch is `expand.py:256-264`:
```python
    if isinstance(proposal, LinkProposal):
        arrow, dropped = _arrow(proposal.link, proposal.source, proposal.target, found)
        return (
            graph.model_copy(update={"links": (*graph.links, arrow)}),
            None,
            (arrow,),
            dropped,
            None,
        )
```

**Lines 2..n — events** (`record.py:629-632`), exactly two keys:

Two things are **not** in the file: `beliefs_propagated` (recomputed from the header seed by `replay.beliefs_of`, replay.py:446-478) and a real receipt (rebuilt to zeroes by `_rebuilt`, replay.py:517-543, keeping only `model`, and taking `recording_date`/`effort`/`prompt_hash` from the header, `mode="replay"`).

`backend/recordings/` currently holds only `.gitkeep` — **there are no committed recordings at `48eb562`**.

`replay.find` — replay.py:370-390:

The hypothesis is read off the recording's own first `generation_started` event (`Recording.hypothesis`, replay.py:172-188). Exact string equality after `strip()`; "Never a nearest match" (replay.py:35-38). Recordings are whole-run, not per-call — there is no per-call cassette keying at all. The scripted intervention matches the same way, on `THE_ONE_THEY_OFFER[example]` letter-for-letter (record.py:133-144).

### What invalidates a recording
Two layers.

`faults_in(recording, *, current_prompt_hash)` — replay.py:607-669 (what CI reads via `check_recordings.main`, and what `record.py:855-868` re-runs on a just-written file before keeping it):

## 9. `proposal.py` — the "validator pipeline"

`proposal.py` itself holds **no pipeline**. Its only executable logic is `Ranged._range_is_ordered` (proposal.py:94-113). Everything else is shape-as-constraint; the module docstring is explicit (proposal.py:38-40): *"If you find yourself writing a check that the model did not do one of the three, the shape is wrong."*

The accept/refuse pipeline, in order:

1. **Shape** — `messages.parse` against `OneProposal`/`StartingClaim`; a miss raises `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` (client.py:481-482) → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:110-120).
2. **Vendor decline** — `Said.declined` → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:122-123).
3. **Wrong shape for the call** — `None`/`StartingClaim` on an expand (expand.py:126-129); non-`LinkProposal` or non-touching link on a join (expand.py:570-591).
4. **`Stop`** → `Stopped`, which is *not* a refusal and puts **no event on the wire** (expand.py:130-131; transcript.py:215-222).
5. **Mint** — `_claim` (id, `Belief(..., owner="model")`, base-rate citation filter) and `_arrow` (id, day-widened lag/half-life, `keep_cited`, `provenance_of`, `reflexive=False` always) — expand.py:282-371.
6. **Map rules** — `newly_wrong(validate(graph), validate(candidate))` → `Refused(violations=...)` or `Accepted` (expand.py:232-238).
7. **Re-judge at the fold** — `still_legal_on` then the width cap → possibly a late `Refused` (grow.py:455-499).

**Event types emitted per proposal** — `events.growth_event`, events.py:317-346:
```python
    result = outcome.result
    if isinstance(result, Accepted):
        return ProposalAccepted(at=at, proposition=result.proposition, links=result.links, frontier=outcome.frontier)
    if not isinstance(result, Refused):
        raise TypeError(...)
    return ProposalRejected(at=at, claim_in_words=result.claim_in_words, violations=result.violations, frontier=outcome.frontier)
```
So: `Accepted` → `proposal_accepted` (events.py:84; `proposition` is `None` for a cross-link, `links` non-empty); `Refused` → `proposal_rejected` (events.py:119, `violations` empty for the non-map refusals); `Stopped` → **no event**, only a `TranscriptLine` with `what="stopped"` (transcript.py:194-196). The `at` counter rises on accepted and rejected only (following.py:109-115), which is why transcript lines can carry `at=None`.

Two details worth flagging for design analysis: `Accepted.sources_dropped` and `Accepted.base_rate_dropped` (outcome.py:142-158) are carried into the transcript (`dropped`, `no_reference_class` — transcript.py:101-118) but onto **no wire event** — the browser never learns which citations were thrown away.</result>

Bounds: `[0,1]` each, plus `lo <= p <= hi`. **This is the only numeric validator in the whole proposal file.**

## 3. The walk driver

**It is `grow.py`, not `following.py`.** `following.py` never decides anything — its contract is "Never decide anything about a map, and never call a model. It reads a walk" (following.py:16). Its loop is:

```python
# following.py:87-98
        try:
            for step in walking:
                if isinstance(step, Finished):
                    self.finished = step
                    break
                self._fold(step)
                if not makes_an_event(step):
                    continue
                yield growth_event(step, self.at - 1)
        except Exception:
            logging.getLogger(__name__).exception(...)
            self.broke = WENT_WRONG
```

### The real loop — `grow()` at `engine/grow.py:124`
1. `start_the_map(hypothesis, is_the_hypothesis=True, ...)` via `_keep_asking` (up to `caps.refusals_in_a_row` = 3 attempts, none told why the last failed) — grow.py:175-201.
2. Optional second `start_the_map(target, is_the_hypothesis=False, ...)` — grow.py:213-230. **The destination never joins the frontier** (comment at grow.py:227-228).
3. The round loop — grow.py:232-274:
```python
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=caps.at_once) as pool:
        while not walk.stopped and walk.frontier:
            if len(graph.propositions) >= caps.claims:
                walk.the_map_is_full()
                break
            room = caps.claims - len(graph.propositions)
            asking = list(walk.frontier[: min(caps.at_once, room)])
            walk.watch(answerer)
            answers = _ask_about_each(pool, graph, asking, target=target, answerer=answerer, on=on,
                                      searches_left=caps.searches - walk.receipt.searches)
            walk.bill(answers)
            waiting = list(zip(asking, answers, strict=True))
            while waiting:
                claim_id, answer = waiting.pop(0)
                graph, outcome = walk.fold(graph, claim_id, answer)
                try:
                    yield outcome.model_copy(update={"frontier": tuple(walk.frontier)})
                except GeneratorExit:
                    ...
```
4. Last ending-only pass — grow.py:279-294: `expand(..., ending_only=True)` per line in `_lines_with_no_ending`, folded with `growing=False`.
5. One `Finished` with `_why_it_stopped` (grow.py:809-832): `spend_cap` > `no_terminal` > whatever closed the last open claim (`claim_cap`/`depth_cap`/`width_cap`/`refusal_cap`) > `reached_terminal`.

### Next-step decision
Frontier is a plain FIFO list. `open_a_line` appends (grow.py:374-377); an accepted claim joins it only if non-terminal:
```python
# grow.py:441-450
            arrived = result.proposition
            if growing and arrived is not None and arrived.kind not in TERMINAL_KINDS:
                self.open_a_line(arrived.id, layer=self.layer[claim_id] + 1)
            if growing:
                self._close_if_out_of_room(graph, claim_id)
                if arrived is not None and arrived.id in self.frontier:
                    self._close_if_out_of_room(graph, arrived.id)
```
Lines close on: `Stopped` (grow.py:420-422, reason `"ended"`), 3 refusals in a row (grow.py:430-434), depth cap, width cap (grow.py:501-516), or `the_map_is_full`.

### Does it ever request a `LinkProposal` / cross-link?

**During the walk: it never *asks* for one specifically, but it will accept one, because every expand call sends the `OneProposal` union.** The only thing that mentions cross-links to the model is the standing text (prompt.py:136-141):
```
What an answer is.
Exactly one of three things:
  a new claim, together with the one arrow that reaches it from a claim already
  on the map;
  an arrow between two claims that are both already on the map;
  or a note that this part of the story is finished, with one sentence saying
  why.
```
`expanding_question` (prompt.py:362-443) never narrows to or toward a link; when the claim is near the start with no step yet it actually pushes the *other* way via `ASK_FOR_A_STEP_FIRST` (prompt.py:436-437, 446-455).

**The dispatch** — `expand.py:122-132`:
```python
    if said.declined is not None:
        return costing(Refused(claim_in_words=said.declined), frontier, said)

    proposed = said.answered
    if proposed is None or isinstance(proposed, StartingClaim):
        return costing(
            Refused(claim_in_words="The model gave no answer to this question."), frontier, said
        )
    if isinstance(proposed, Stop):
        return costing(Stopped(why=proposed.why), frontier, said)
    return costing(_judge(graph, proposed, found_in(said, on=on)), frontier, said)
```
i.e. anything that is a `ClaimProposal` **or** a `LinkProposal` falls through to `_judge`. The link branch is `expand.py:256-264`:
```python
    if isinstance(proposal, LinkProposal):
        arrow, dropped = _arrow(proposal.link, proposal.source, proposal.target, found)
        return (
            graph.model_copy(update={"links": (*graph.links, arrow)}),
            None,
            (arrow,),
            dropped,
            None,
        )
```
A link-only acceptance then has `result.proposition is None`, so `grow.fold` adds nothing to the frontier and the claim it was asked about stays open (or closes by width).

**The only place a `LinkProposal` is *required*** is `expand_toward` (expand.py:537-592), reachable only from `add_a_claim` (expand.py:448-534), which is the "Add a claim" edit — reached from `record.py:330` (scripted intervention) and the insert API route, **not** from `grow()`:
```python
# expand.py:570-591
    if not isinstance(proposed, LinkProposal):
        return costing(
            Refused(claim_in_words=("This call asked for one arrow between two claims already on the "
                                    "map, and the answer was something else.")), added, said)
    if added not in (proposed.source, proposed.target):
        return costing(
            Refused(claim_in_words=("This arrow does not touch the claim that was just added, so it "
                                    "is not part of adding it.")), added, said)
```

**Where a deliberate walk-time cross-link request would go:** a new branch in `grow()`'s round loop (around grow.py:243-253) choosing a different `expand_*` call, plus a new varying-half builder in `prompt.py` beside `joining_question` (prompt.py:312-359 — which already does exactly this shape of ask), plus a dispatch arm in `expand.py`. Nothing today selects candidate pairs.

## 4. `prompt.py`

**Assembly.** Two halves. Standing half = the module constant `STANDING_TEXT` (prompt.py:47-146), sent byte-identical as `STANDING_BLOCK` (client.py:141-151) with `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}`. Varying half = one of four builders, always sent as the single user message:
- `starting_question(sentence, *, is_the_hypothesis, today)` — prompt.py:188
- `adding_question(graph, sentence, *, today)` — prompt.py:264
- `joining_question(graph, added, *, today)` — prompt.py:312
- `expanding_question(graph, frontier, *, target, ending_only, today)` — prompt.py:362

Each starts with `_today(today)` (prompt.py:530) and, where a map is shown, `_map_as_text(graph)` (prompt.py:501-527): claims sorted by id as `  {id}  {claim}` (+ `" (this is what the person expects)"` for the hypothesis), then arrows sorted by `(source, target, id)` as `  {source} -> {target}`. **No likelihoods are shown** ("A model shown its own earlier numbers anchors on them", prompt.py:511-513).

**Prompt fingerprint** — `prompt_hash()` at prompt.py:154:
```python
    from katalyst.engine.client import what_goes_out

    shapes = json.dumps(what_goes_out(), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256((STANDING_TEXT + shapes).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
```
`what_goes_out()` (client.py:188-203) returns `{"proposal": wire_schema(OneProposal), "starting_claim": wire_schema(StartingClaim)}`, where `wire_schema` is `transform_schema(TypeAdapter(shape).json_schema())` (client.py:206-222) — i.e. **the schema as the library actually transmits it**, so every field description and every docstring is inside the hash (see the warning at client.py:180-185: a docstring edit "invalidates every cassette and changes the prompt's fingerprint").

It deliberately **excludes the varying half** (prompt.py:168-170) — so map contents, today's date and the target never change it.

Used at: `following.py:194` (on the live `Receipt` event), `record.py:573` (`KeptRun.prompt_hash`), `record.py:615` (recording header), `record.py:868` and `check_recordings.py:38,45` (fault check), compared at `replay.py:664`.

**Which sections mention what**
- **Base rates / outside view**: `STANDING_TEXT` "Start from the outside, then come inside." (prompt.py:85-98) — "**Search for it.**… Stop searching as soon as you have a countable set with a page behind it… A count you cannot point at a page for is worse than no count". Also `starting_question` prompt.py:250-253 and `adding_question` prompt.py:305-307.
- **Causes / parents**: `STANDING_TEXT` prompt.py:143-145 ("You never name a new claim with anything but its words. The short names in the map we show you are ours; point at one when you name a cause"); `expanding_question` prompt.py:405-406 ("use one when you name a cause"); `joining_question` prompt.py:348-350 ("It may cause something already on the map, or something already on the map may cause it"). "Parents", plural, never appears.
- **Inhibitors / falsifiers / necessary conditions / blockers**: **absent from the entire codebase.** A grep for `inhibit|falsif|parent|necessary condition|blocker` across `src/katalyst/**.py` returns only unrelated branch-`parent` hits in `worlds.py`/`patch.py`/`hormuz.py` and `Path.parents`. Direction of push is carried only by the sign of `LinkDraft.strength` and by `mode`.
- **Endings/trade**: prompt.py:122-133; **citations**: prompt.py:110-116; **claim standing alone**: prompt.py:69-76.

## 5. `expand.py` — validation, refusals, reason codes

No split modules. Entry points:
- `expand(graph, frontier, *, target, answerer, on, may_search, ending_only)` — expand.py:76. One walk step.
- `start_the_map(sentence, *, is_the_hypothesis, answerer, on, may_search)` — expand.py:135.
- `add_a_claim(graph, sentence, *, answerer, on, width, may_search, dollars)` — expand.py:448. One `_drafted` call + up to `width` `expand_toward` calls.
- `expand_toward(...)` — expand.py:537. One cross-link between existing claims.
- Minters: `_starting_claim` (192), `_claim` (282), `_arrow` (334).
- Graph helpers used by `grow.py`: `map_with` (374), `still_legal_on` (397), `newly_wrong` (415).

**Where proposals are validated** — `_judge`, expand.py:215-238:
```python
    candidate, claim, arrows, dropped, no_class = _candidate_map(graph, proposal, found)
    introduced = newly_wrong(validate(graph), validate(candidate))
    if introduced:
        return Refused(claim_in_words=_in_the_models_words(proposal), violations=introduced)
    return Accepted(proposition=claim, links=arrows, sources_dropped=dropped, base_rate_dropped=no_class)
```
Only *newly introduced* faults count (`newly_wrong`, expand.py:415-426). **Second validation** at fold time via `still_legal_on` (expand.py:397-412) called from `grow._Walk._judged_again` (grow.py:455-499), which then also applies the per-source width cap via `out_of_room_beside` (grow.py:583-611).

**Where refusals are emitted**

| Site | Trigger | Violations |
|---|---|---|
| expand.py:110-120 | `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` / `TheModelDidNotAnswer`; `calls=1`, tokens 0 | none |
| expand.py:122-123 | `said.declined` (vendor safety refusal) | none |
| expand.py:126-129 | `answered is None` or a `StartingClaim` on an expand call | none |
| expand.py:235 | `domain.validate` found new faults | **yes, the `ViolationCode`s** |
| expand.py:175-185 | same three, on `start_the_map` | none |
| expand.py:562-591 | `expand_toward`: not a `LinkProposal`; or arrow doesn't touch the added claim | none |
| expand.py:602-610 | `_drafted` failures | none |
| grow.py:476-485 | late re-judge failed | yes |
| grow.py:486-498 | width cap ("There is no room beside …") | none |
| grow.py:731-739 | `_never_answered` — an exception the seam didn't convert | none |

**Refusal reason codes** = `ViolationCode`, `domain/validity.py:43-64` — 20 stable strings:
`missing_resolution, missing_rationale, documented_without_source, cycle, reflexive_without_lag, half_life_without_impulse, impulse_without_half_life, belief_out_of_range, no_terminal, no_hypothesis, multiple_hypotheses, dangling_link, duplicate_link, market_without_payoff, not_tradeable_without_reason, unknown_target, unknown_link, duplicate_id, edit_not_applicable, worlds_not_comparable`.
The first 15 are map faults from `validate`; the last 5 are edit/comparison refusals no map can carry. Cross-link-relevant ones: `cycle` (validity.py:674) and `duplicate_link` (validity.py:526 — "The **first** arrow between a pair is never the fault").
Everything else refuses with **empty `violations` and prose only** in `Refused.claim_in_words` — there is no code namespace for those.

## 6. `grounding.py` — sources and provenance

Three pure functions plus a normaliser; imports only `domain.{Provenance, Source}`, `outcome.Said`, `proposal.LinkDraft`.

- `found_in(said, *, on) -> tuple[Source, ...]` — grounding.py:37. **The only place a `Source` is built during generation:**
  ```python
  return tuple(Source(url=page.url, title=page.title, retrieved=on) for page in said.found)
  ```
  `said.found` is `tuple[FoundPage, ...]`, populated exclusively from `web_search_tool_result` blocks in `client._pages_the_search_returned` (client.py:567-597), deduped by url in first-seen order. A failed search yields an error object where the result list would be and reads as nothing found.
- `keep_cited(cited, found) -> (kept, dropped)` — grounding.py:58. Exact url match after `same_address` (strip + one trailing slash removed, grounding.py:127-144). Dropped addresses are never repaired or fetched. Used twice: for a link's `SourceDraft.url`s (expand.py:356) and for `BaseRate.sources` (expand.py:312).
- `provenance_of(draft, kept)` — grounding.py:98: `"documented"` if any kept source; else `"argued"` if `draft.rationale.strip()`; else `"asserted"`.

**Fields that end up on `Source`** (`domain/link.py:53-81`): `url: str`, `title: str`, `retrieved: date | None`. That is all.

**Is any passage/quote/locator captured today? No.** Nothing in the pipeline reads search-result body text. `FoundPage` is only `url` + `title` (outcome.py:39-53), and `SourceDraft` is only `url`. The gap is flagged as an open question in the type itself, `domain/link.py:63-65`:
```python
    # Open question 2 in spec/graph/link.md: these three fields are a proposal.
    # Does a source also need a publisher, a quoted snippet, or an access date
    # separate from the day we fetched it?
```
`BaseRate.sources` is even thinner — bare `tuple[str, ...]` of urls (`domain/proposition.py:96`), with its own open-question comment at proposition.py:93-95. A base rate whose citations all get dropped is discarded whole, and only its `reference_class` string survives as `Accepted.base_rate_dropped` (expand.py:311-319).

## 7. `record.py` + `replay.py` — the recording format

### File format
`backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, written at `record.py:589-638`.

**Line 1 — header** (`record.py:610-624`), keys exactly:
```python
    header = {
        "base_id": "" if built is None else built.id,
        "effort": run.effort,
        "seed": run.seed,
        "recording_date": run.on.isoformat(),
        "prompt_hash": prompt_hash(),
        "insert": (None if run.scripted_insert is None else {
                "claim_in_words": THE_ONE_THEY_OFFER[run.example],
                "answer": json.loads(run.scripted_insert.model_dump_json()),
            }),
    }
```
Parsed by `RecordingHeader` (replay.py:115-149). Note `insert` is typed **non-optional** there (`insert: RecordedInsert`), so a `None` makes the file unreadable by design.

**Lines 2..n — events** (`record.py:629-632`), exactly two keys:
```python
                json.dumps({"event": events.name_of(one), "data": json.loads(one.model_dump_json())})
```
`events.NAMES` (events.py:266-275) is the closed name set: `generation_started, proposal_accepted, proposal_rejected, beliefs_propagated, verdict, receipt, done, failed`.

Two things are **not** in the file: `beliefs_propagated` (recomputed from the header seed by `replay.beliefs_of`, replay.py:446-478) and a real receipt (rebuilt to zeroes by `_rebuilt`, replay.py:517-543, keeping only `model`, and taking `recording_date`/`effort`/`prompt_hash` from the header, `mode="replay"`).

`backend/recordings/` currently holds only `.gitkeep` — **there are no committed recordings at `48eb562`**.

### How a recorded call is matched — **not by prompt fingerprint**
`replay.find` — replay.py:370-390:
```python
    wanted = hypothesis.strip()
    for one in every_recording(folder):
        if one.hypothesis.strip() == wanted:
            return one
    return None
```
The hypothesis is read off the recording's own first `generation_started` event (`Recording.hypothesis`, replay.py:172-188). Exact string equality after `strip()`; "Never a nearest match" (replay.py:35-38). Recordings are whole-run, not per-call — there is no per-call cassette keying at all. The scripted intervention matches the same way, on `THE_ONE_THEY_OFFER[example]` letter-for-letter (record.py:133-144).

### What invalidates a recording
Two layers.

`faults_in(recording, *, current_prompt_hash)` — replay.py:607-669 (what CI reads via `check_recordings.main`, and what `record.py:855-868` re-runs on a just-written file before keeping it):
1. event name not in `events.BY_NAME`;
2. any event payload failing `shape.model_validate`;
3. first event is not `generation_started`;
4. last event is not `done`;
5. `beliefs_propagated` present (stored likelihoods are forbidden);
6. `_grammar_faults` (replay.py:555-604): receipt not second-to-last; growth events after the verdict; `at` counters not a strictly rising line, or non-numeric;
7. filename not in `THE_FOUR_EXAMPLES = ("export-controls","hormuz","midterms","photonics")`;
8. a `proposal_rejected` with neither violations nor `claim_in_words`;
9. **`recording.header.prompt_hash != current_prompt_hash`** → "was made against a different prompt from the one shipping today… Record it again." (replay.py:664-668).
`check_recordings.py:47-52` adds a tenth: two recordings from the same sentence.

Separately, at read/play time: `read` raises `CannotBeRead` for an empty file or anything that won't parse (replay.py:209-238), and `why_it_cannot_be_played` (replay.py:241-272) rejects a file that reads but holds an unknown event or a payload that won't validate — `readable()` uses that to decide which cards the launchpad may offer, while `every_recording()` is deliberately more forgiving.

Run-level gate before a recording is even written: `faults_of(run)` — record.py:495-539: stopped on `spend_cap`; the run broke; `KATALYST_ANSWERER` was set (a stand-in run "is a recording of nothing"); no finished graph; no `Done`; no scripted insert. Explicitly **not** a fault: a run with zero refusals (record.py:501-510).

## 8. `client.py` — model, tokens, retries, streaming, cost

- **Model names**: default from `settings.KATALYST_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5"` (`settings.py:78`), overridable per-`Model` (client.py:387) or via `--model` (record.py:788-787). Priced models, `pricing.py:97-102`: `claude-sonnet-5` (in $2.00/M, out $10.00/M, cacheable from 1024 tok) and `claude-opus-5` (in $5.00/M, out $25.00/M, cacheable from 512). `prices_for` raises `KeyError` rather than guessing (pricing.py:118-139).
- **Max tokens**: `ROOM_FOR_AN_ANSWER = 16_000` (client.py:66), passed as `max_tokens=` (client.py:468).
- **Temperature / top_p / top_k**: **never set.** Grep over `engine/*.py` finds no occurrence. ## 9. `proposal.py` — the "validator pipeline"

`proposal.py` itself holds **no pipeline**. Its only executable logic is `Ranged._range_is_ordered` (proposal.py:94-113). Everything else is shape-as-constraint; the module docstring is explicit (proposal.py:38-40): *"If you find yourself writing a check that the model did not do one of the three, the shape is wrong."*

The accept/refuse pipeline, in order:

1. **Shape** — `messages.parse` against `OneProposal`/`StartingClaim`; a miss raises `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` (client.py:481-482) → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:110-120).
2. **Vendor decline** — `Said.declined` → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:122-123).
3. **Wrong shape for the call** — `None`/`StartingClaim` on an expand (expand.py:126-129); non-`LinkProposal` or non-touching link on a join (expand.py:570-591).
4. **`Stop`** → `Stopped`, which is *not* a refusal and puts **no event on the wire** (expand.py:130-131; transcript.py:215-222).
5. **Mint** — `_claim` (id, `Belief(..., owner="model")`, base-rate citation filter) and `_arrow` (id, day-widened lag/half-life, `keep_cited`, `provenance_of`, `reflexive=False` always) — expand.py:282-371.
6. **Map rules** — `newly_wrong(validate(graph), validate(candidate))` → `Refused(violations=...)` or `Accepted` (expand.py:232-238).
7. **Re-judge at the fold** — `still_legal_on` then the width cap → possibly a late `Refused` (grow.py:455-499).

**Event types emitted per proposal** — `events.growth_event`, events.py:317-346:
```python
    result = outcome.result
    if isinstance(result, Accepted):
        return ProposalAccepted(at=at, proposition=result.proposition, links=result.links, frontier=outcome.frontier)
    if not isinstance(result, Refused):
        raise TypeError(...)
    return ProposalRejected(at=at, claim_in_words=result.claim_in_words, violations=result.violations, frontier=outcome.frontier)
```
So: `Accepted` → `proposal_accepted` (events.py:84; `proposition` is `None` for a cross-link, `links` non-empty); `Refused` → `proposal_rejected` (events.py:119, `violations` empty for the non-map refusals); `Stopped` → **no event**, only a `TranscriptLine` with `what="stopped"` (transcript.py:194-196). ## 6. `grounding.py` — sources and provenance

Three pure functions plus a normaliser; imports only `domain.{Provenance, Source}`, `outcome.Said`, `proposal.LinkDraft`.

- `found_in(said, *, on) -> tuple[Source, ...]` — grounding.py:37. **The only place a `Source` is built during generation:**
  ```python
  return tuple(Source(url=page.url, title=page.title, retrieved=on) for page in said.found)
  ```
  `said.found` is `tuple[FoundPage, ...]`, populated exclusively from `web_search_tool_result` blocks in `client._pages_the_search_returned` (client.py:567-597), deduped by url in first-seen order. A failed search yields an error object where the result list would be and reads as nothing found.
- `keep_cited(cited, found) -> (kept, dropped)` — grounding.py:58. Exact url match after `same_address` (strip + one trailing slash removed, grounding.py:127-144). Dropped addresses are never repaired or fetched. Used twice: for a link's `SourceDraft.url`s (expand.py:356) and for `BaseRate.sources` (expand.py:312).
- `provenance_of(draft, kept)` — grounding.py:98: `"documented"` if any kept source; else `"argued"` if `draft.rationale.strip()`; else `"asserted"`.

**Fields that end up on `Source`** (`domain/link.py:53-81`): `url: str`, `title: str`, `retrieved: date | None`. That is all.

**Is any passage/quote/locator captured today? No.** Nothing in the pipeline reads search-result body text. `FoundPage` is only `url` + `title` (outcome.py:39-53), and `SourceDraft` is only `url`. The gap is flagged as an open question in the type itself, `domain/link.py:63-65`:
```python

    # Does a source also need a publisher, a quoted snippet, or an access date
    # separate from the day we fetched it?
```
`BaseRate.sources` is even thinner — bare `tuple[str, ...]` of urls (`domain/proposition.py:96`), with its own open-question comment at proposition.py:93-95. A base rate whose citations all get dropped is discarded whole, and only its `reference_class` string survives as `Accepted.base_rate_dropped` (expand.py:311-319).

## 7. `record.py` + `replay.py` — the recording format

### File format
`backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, written at `record.py:589-638`.

**Line 1 — header** (`record.py:610-624`), keys exactly:
```python
    header = {
        "base_id": "" if built is None else built.id,
        "effort": run.effort,
        "seed": run.seed,
        "recording_date": run.on.isoformat(),
        "prompt_hash": prompt_hash(),
        "insert": (None if run.scripted_insert is None else {
                "claim_in_words": THE_ONE_THEY_OFFER[run.example],
                "answer": json.loads(run.scripted_insert.model_dump_json()),
            }),
    }
```
Parsed by `RecordingHeader` (replay.py:115-149). Note `insert` is typed **non-optional** there (`insert: RecordedInsert`), so a `None` makes the file unreadable by design.

**Lines 2..n — events** (`record.py:629-632`), exactly two keys:
```python
                json.dumps({"event": events.name_of(one), "data": json.loads(one.model_dump_json())})
```
`events.NAMES` (events.py:266-275) is the closed name set: `generation_started, proposal_accepted, proposal_rejected, beliefs_propagated, verdict, receipt, done, failed`.

Two things are **not** in the file: `beliefs_propagated` (recomputed from the header seed by `replay.beliefs_of`, replay.py:446-478) and a real receipt (rebuilt to zeroes by `_rebuilt`, replay.py:517-543, keeping only `model`, and taking `recording_date`/`effort`/`prompt_hash` from the header, `mode="replay"`).

`backend/recordings/` currently holds only `.gitkeep` — **there are no committed recordings at `48eb562`**.

### How a recorded call is matched — **not by prompt fingerprint**
`replay.find` — replay.py:370-390:
```python
    wanted = hypothesis.strip()
    for one in every_recording(folder):
        if one.hypothesis.strip() == wanted:
            return one
    return None
```
The hypothesis is read off the recording's own first `generation_started` event (`Recording.hypothesis`, replay.py:172-188). Exact string equality after `strip()`; "Never a nearest match" (replay.py:35-38). Recordings are whole-run, not per-call — there is no per-call cassette keying at all. The scripted intervention matches the same way, on `THE_ONE_THEY_OFFER[example]` letter-for-letter (record.py:133-144).

### What invalidates a recording
Two layers.

`faults_in(recording, *, current_prompt_hash)` — replay.py:607-669 (what CI reads via `check_recordings.main`, and what `record.py:855-868` re-runs on a just-written file before keeping it):
1. event name not in `events.BY_NAME`;
2. any event payload failing `shape.model_validate`;
3. first event is not `generation_started`;
4. last event is not `done`;
5. `beliefs_propagated` present (stored likelihoods are forbidden);
6. `_grammar_faults` (replay.py:555-604): receipt not second-to-last; growth events after the verdict; `at` counters not a strictly rising line, or non-numeric;
7. filename not in `THE_FOUR_EXAMPLES = ("export-controls","hormuz","midterms","photonics")`;
8. a `proposal_rejected` with neither violations nor `claim_in_words`;
9. **`recording.header.prompt_hash != current_prompt_hash`** → "was made against a different prompt from the one shipping today… Record it again." (replay.py:664-668).
`check_recordings.py:47-52` adds a tenth: two recordings from the same sentence.

Separately, at read/play time: `read` raises `CannotBeRead` for an empty file or anything that won't parse (replay.py:209-238), and `why_it_cannot_be_played` (replay.py:241-272) rejects a file that reads but holds an unknown event or a payload that won't validate — `readable()` uses that to decide which cards the launchpad may offer, while `every_recording()` is deliberately more forgiving.

Run-level gate before a recording is even written: `faults_of(run)` — record.py:495-539: stopped on `spend_cap`; the run broke; `KATALYST_ANSWERER` was set (a stand-in run "is a recording of nothing"); no finished graph; no `Done`; no scripted insert. Explicitly **not** a fault: a run with zero refusals (record.py:501-510).

- **Model names**: default from `settings.KATALYST_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5"` (`settings.py:78`), overridable per-`Model` (client.py:387) or via `--model` (record.py:788-787). - **Temperature / top_p / top_k**: **never set.** Grep over `engine/*.py` finds no occurrence. - **Retries**: `HOW_OFTEN_TO_TRY_AGAIN = 2` (client.py:266), passed as `max_retries=` (client.py:719). These are **the library's own silent retries** — 408/409/429/5xx/connection failures. Distinct from the *proposal*-level retry: `caps.refusals_in_a_row = 3` in `grow.py`, where the same question is re-asked up to 3 times and never told why (engine/__init__.py:11-13).

## 9. `proposal.py` — the "validator pipeline"

`proposal.py` itself holds **no pipeline**. Its only executable logic is `Ranged._range_is_ordered` (proposal.py:94-113). Everything else is shape-as-constraint; the module docstring is explicit (proposal.py:38-40): *"If you find yourself writing a check that the model did not do one of the three, the shape is wrong."*

The accept/refuse pipeline, in order:

1. **Shape** — `messages.parse` against `OneProposal`/`StartingClaim`; a miss raises `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` (client.py:481-482) → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:110-120).
2. **Vendor decline** — `Said.declined` → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:122-123).
3. **Wrong shape for the call** — `None`/`StartingClaim` on an expand (expand.py:126-129); non-`LinkProposal` or non-touching link on a join (expand.py:570-591).
4. **`Stop`** → `Stopped`, which is *not* a refusal and puts **no event on the wire** (expand.py:130-131; transcript.py:215-222).
5. **Mint** — `_claim` (id, `Belief(..., owner="model")`, base-rate citation filter) and `_arrow` (id, day-widened lag/half-life, `keep_cited`, `provenance_of`, `reflexive=False` always) — expand.py:282-371.
6. **Map rules** — `newly_wrong(validate(graph), validate(candidate))` → `Refused(violations=...)` or `Accepted` (expand.py:232-238).
7. **Re-judge at the fold** — `still_legal_on` then the width cap → possibly a late `Refused` (grow.py:455-499).

**Event types emitted per proposal** — `events.growth_event`, events.py:317-346:
```python
    result = outcome.result
    if isinstance(result, Accepted):
        return ProposalAccepted(at=at, proposition=result.proposition, links=result.links, frontier=outcome.frontier)
    if not isinstance(result, Refused):
        raise TypeError(...)
    return ProposalRejected(at=at, claim_in_words=result.claim_in_words, violations=result.violations, frontier=outcome.frontier)
```
So: `Accepted` → `proposal_accepted` (events.py:84; `proposition` is `None` for a cross-link, `links` non-empty); `Refused` → `proposal_rejected` (events.py:119, `violations` empty for the non-map refusals); `Stopped` → **no event**, only a `TranscriptLine` with `what="stopped"` (transcript.py:194-196). The `at` counter rises on accepted and rejected only (following.py:109-115), which is why transcript lines can carry `at=None`.

Two details worth flagging for design analysis: `Accepted.sources_dropped` and `Accepted.base_rate_dropped` (outcome.py:142-158) are carried into the transcript (`dropped`, `no_reference_class` — transcript.py:101-118) but onto **no wire event** — the browser never learns which citations were thrown away.</result>

## 1A. The empirical framing (§3 preamble, lines 47)

> "The empirical picture: scaffolded, retrieval-augmented LLMs approach crowd-aggregate accuracy ([Halawi et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18563)), and LLM *ensembles* are statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd on small question sets ([Schoenegger et al., Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adp1528)) — but on a leakage-free, continuously-refreshed benchmark superforecasters still beat the best LLM by Brier 0.068 vs 0.119 ([ForecastBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19839)), several times the GPT-4→GPT-4o gap. The popular read ([ACX](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here)) is that scaffolds are worth about a model generation and finance-adjacent questions are where AI does relatively *best*. Encouraging — but the scaffold is doing the work, not the model."

Numbers with citations: Brier **0.068** (superforecasters) vs **0.119** (best LLM), ForecastBench (arXiv 2409.19839). Qualifier attached: "statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd **on small question sets**"; ForecastBench is "**leakage-free, continuously-refreshed**" — i.e. the author is explicitly weighting the leakage-free benchmark above the parity results.

## 1B. Base rate first, then adjust (§3, item 1, line 51)

> "**Base rate before narrative.** Elicit the reference class and its historical frequency in a *separate call that has not seen the scenario*, then adjust in a second call. Merging them invites representativeness: a vivid chain scores high because it is a good *story*."

Key operational detail: **two separate calls**, and the base-rate call must **not have seen the scenario**. No citation attached to this item (the supporting literature is representativeness/Kahneman, invoked by name only).

## 1C. Conditionals, never joints (§3, item 2, line 52)

> "**Elicit conditionals, never joints.** Ask for `P(B|A)` and `P(B|¬A)`; compute the rest. Humans and LLMs both violate the conjunction rule — a detailed conjunction is judged *more* likely than its own conjunct ([Tversky & Kahneman 1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunction_fallacy)). A five-step chain at 0.8 per step is 0.33, and the model will call it "very likely" if allowed."

Worked number: **0.8^5 = 0.33** for a five-step chain. Citation: Tversky & Kahneman 1983 (linked to the Wikipedia conjunction-fallacy page, not the paper).

## 1D. Small ensembles, k samples, geometric mean of odds, dispersion (§3, item 3, line 53)

> "**Sample k ≥ 5 times** across prompt variants and ideally two model families, then **aggregate by geometric mean of odds** ([summary](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/sMjcjnnpoAQCcedL2/when-pooling-forecasts-use-the-geometric-mean-of-odds)). **Keep the spread**: dispersion across independent elicitations is a defensible first-order estimate of that parameter's uncertainty, feeding §4 at zero extra cost."

Three separable claims: (a) **k ≥ 5**, varied over **prompt variants** and **ideally two model families**; (b) aggregate by **geometric mean of odds**; (c) **retain the dispersion** as the parameter's uncertainty.

Note on evidentiary status: the geometric-mean-of-odds link is an **EA Forum post** ("summary"), not a peer-reviewed source. **`k ≥ 5` carries no citation** — it is the author's judgement. Median and arithmetic mean are **not discussed anywhere in the document**; geometric mean of odds is asserted as the aggregator without a stated comparison against the alternatives. This is a gap if the parent agent expected a median-vs-geomean-vs-arithmetic argument.

## 1E. Do not extremize (§3, item 4, line 54)

> "**Do not extremize by default.** Extremizing helps for independent human forecasters ([discussion](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/biL94PKfeHmgHY6qe/principled-extremizing-of-aggregated-forecasts)), but LLM samples are highly correlated and chain errors compound multiplicatively. Here it manufactures confidence."

The stated reason extremizing transfers badly: **LLM samples are highly correlated** (violating the independence premise) **and** chain errors **compound multiplicatively**. Citation is again an EA Forum post, and it is cited *for the positive result in humans*, i.e. the document's own recommendation runs against its cited source, on an uncited mechanistic argument.

## 1F. Known LLM pathologies / calibration correction (§3, item 5, line 55)

> "**Correct known LLM pathologies**: RLHF pushes models toward confident-sounding outputs ([Taming Overconfidence in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09724)), and verbalized probabilities cluster on round numbers and avoid the tails. Force explicit `<1%` / `>99%` options; add a per-model recalibration map once questions resolve."

Two concrete mechanisms: **forced `<1%` / `>99%` response options**, and a **per-model recalibration map built from resolved questions**. Citation covers only the RLHF-overconfidence half; the **round-number clustering / tail avoidance claim is uncited inline** (`Just Ask for Calibration`, arXiv 2305.14975, appears only in the source list at line 163, never invoked in the body).

## 1G. Coherence / consistency checks (§3, lines 57–62)

> "**Coherence checks to run automatically** (all cheap, all blocking):
>
> - Marginal consistency: `P(B) ≈ P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|¬A)P(¬A)` vs. a directly-elicited `P(B)`; flag >10pp divergence.
> - Relevance: an edge is justified only if `P(B|A) ≠ P(B|¬A)`. Equal values → delete the edge.
> - Symmetry of dependence: `P(B|A) > P(B)` iff `P(A|B) > P(A)`.
> - Chain sanity: compare the model's *verbal* summary ("highly likely") against the computed number and show the conflict. This is the anti-conjunction-fallacy feature, and a genuinely good product moment."

All four are **blocking**, not advisory. The threshold **>10pp** is uncited/author-chosen. Note the fourth check is framed as both a rigor mechanism and **a product moment** — verbal-vs-computed conflict surfaced to the user.

## 1H. Elicitation units — odds ratios, not probabilities (§2, line 39)

> "**Recommendation: signed log-odds as the default, with leaky noisy-OR and noisy-AND per node.** It handles inhibition, which noisy-OR cannot; elicitation is in odds ratios ("~3× more likely"), which forecasters can produce; each edge's contribution is `wᵢ` in bits, so the inspector gets "this edge moved the target +1.2 bits" free…"

Directly relevant to elicitation design: ask the model for a **signed odds ratio ("~3× more likely")**, not a raw probability. Parameter counts: logistic link = **`k + 1` numbers** (line 37); leaky noisy-OR = **`k + 1` numbers** (line 34); full CPT = **`2^k` rows, 16 numbers at k = 4** (line 32), elicited from "a model that will produce non-monotone, mutually incoherent rows."

Also from §2 (line 41), a constraint on elicited numbers: "**saturation** (clip and warn past ~0.99)."

## 1I. Dispersion → a range, not a point (§4, line 70)

> "**Monte Carlo over parameters → a band, not a point.** Draw each parameter from its across-sample dispersion (§3.3) ~1,000 times and re-run inference. ~20 lines, and the strongest antidote to false precision: the band visibly widens with chain length, which is the honest lesson."

**~1,000 draws**, parameter distributions sourced directly from the k-sample spread of §3.3. Explicitly rejected alternative (line 75):

> "**Skip imprecise probability / credal networks.** Interval propagation is exponential in practice, the intervals go vacuously wide, and no user can interpret them. Parameter MC captures ~90% of the honesty at ~5% of the cost."

The **~90% / ~5%** figures are rhetorical, uncited.

Related, §4 item 2 (line 71): "**One-way sensitivity / tornado.** Perturb each parameter over its plausible range, rank by target movement… `2 × #params` inferences — milliseconds here. Tells the user *which single number their thesis rests on*."

## 1J. Base rates as leak terms — elicited, never defaulted (§5, line 87)

> "**Structural uncertainty is the dominant error term, and the leak is where it lives.** Every node's "no parents active" probability must be *elicited as a base rate*, never defaulted to zero; a zero leak asserts the LLM's cause list is exhaustive, which it never is. Disclose per graph that the computed number is a lower bound if the enumerated causes are only some of the causes."

## 1K. Provenance of raw samples — keeping the k (§6, line 95)

> "**Provenance per node and edge**: source URLs with retrieval timestamps, model, prompt version, elicitation method, and the k raw samples *before* aggregation. Without the raw samples you cannot distinguish "the model was confident" from "the models disagreed and we averaged"."

## 1L. Calibration and scoring (§6, lines 96–99)

> "**Immutable snapshots.** Every published chain is frozen and timestamped so it can be scored later. A forecast you can silently edit is not a forecast."

> "**Proper scoring rules.** Brier for the user-facing calibration view; log score alongside, since it punishes confident errors — the failure mode that matters here. Always report a **skill score** relative to the elicited base rate; absolute Brier on easy questions flatters everyone."

> "**Score sub-claims, not just the target.** A chain that lands the right answer through compensating errors must be flagged. Node-level scoring is what makes a chain falsifiable rather than merely narratable."

## 1M. The elicitation service, condensed (§(a) item 6, line 118)

> "**Elicitation service**: base-rate-first, conditionals-only, k samples, geometric mean of odds, dispersion retained as parameter uncertainty."

Plus item 10 (line 122): "**Scoring ledger**: frozen snapshots, node-level resolution, Brier + log score + skill vs. base rate, **per-model calibration curve**."

## 1N. Tests that detect bad elicitation (§(b), lines 130–132)

Trap 5 — LLM-stated joint probabilities:
> "*Test:* inspect the prompts — is the model ever asked for the probability of a whole path or of the target given the story? Is the displayed path probability computed or generated? **Re-run one edge twice; if the stored number moves, it is a single unaggregated sample.**"

Trap 6 — Narrative swamping the base rate:
> "*Test:* build a chain ending in a rare, documented event ("S&P 500 falls >20% in a quarter", historically a few percent). With no assumptions applied, is the unconditional endpoint anywhere near that? If it reads 30%, the story is driving the number."

Trap 7 — False precision:
> "*Test:* move one edge from `P(B|A) = 0.6` to `0.45` and see whether the headline conclusion flips. If it does and the UI never flagged that edge as load-bearing, the audit story is broken. **Any figure past two significant digits is theatre.**"

Trap 8 — Non-falsifiable nodes: "*Test:* **sample 10 generated nodes** and apply the clarity test — date, source, judgement-free resolution — and record the failure fraction."

> "**A chat agent that answers the question directly.** The graph must be the artefact; a chatbot that emits a probability reintroduces every pathology in §3."

## 1P. What the cited literature supports vs. does not — my read of the document

Supported by the cited work:
- LLM/crowd near-parity on small sets and with scaffolding (Halawi; Schoenegger, *Science Advances*).
- A real, several-times-a-model-generation residual gap to superforecasters on leakage-free questions (ForecastBench, 0.068 vs 0.119).
- Conjunction-rule violation in humans (Tversky & Kahneman 1983).
- RLHF-induced overconfidence (arXiv 2410.09724).
- Extremizing helps for **independent human** forecasters (EA Forum) — note this supports the opposite of the document's recommendation for the LLM case.
- LLMs recall rather than discover causal claims — both the optimistic (Kıcıman) and pessimistic (Zečević, *Causal Parrots*) papers "agree the model is *recalling* causal claims from text, not discovering them" (line 22).

**Not** supported by any cited source in this document (author judgement, flagged as such):
- `k ≥ 5` specifically, and "ideally two model families."
- Geometric mean of odds over median or arithmetic mean — asserted via an EA Forum summary; **no comparison to median or arithmetic mean appears in the document at all**.
- Dispersion across elicitations as a valid uncertainty estimate ("a defensible first-order estimate" — argued, not evidenced).
- The **>10pp** marginal-consistency threshold.
- Round-number clustering / tail avoidance in verbalized probabilities (inline uncited).
- The ~1,000 MC draws and the "~90% of the honesty at ~5% of the cost" tradeoff.
- The entire §3 protocol as a *sequence* — it is a synthesis, not a replicated finding.

## 2A. Metaculus — resolvable propositions, conditional pairs, annulment (§1, line 9–11)

> "**Metaculus** — an event is not a phrase, it is a *resolvable proposition*. A question is title + background + **resolution criteria** + fine print + dates, and the criteria are load-bearing: they *"should stand on its own as a set of self-contained instructions"* and supersede the background ([FAQ](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/)). Fine print is a deliberate readability valve; questions pass an [approval checklist](https://www.metaculus.com/help/question-checklist/) before going live, because an ambiguous criterion poisons every forecast attached to it."

> "The relevant primitive is the **Conditional Pair**: "if the Parent resolves Yes, how does the Child resolve?" and "if No?", asked together. In the feed each Parent outcome is an **arrow** and each conditional probability a **bar** — a two-branch fork glyph; in the forecasting UI it is a table, or `IF YES` / `IF NO` buttons opening distribution editors. It exists because *"two forecasters could have the same forecasts… while having very different mental models of their relationship"* ([announcement](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nQhmiKeYPvFaEZfWc/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions)). **The gap between branches *is* the causal claim** — the unit of value is P(B|A) − P(B|¬A), not P(B|A). One more detail worth copying: when the Parent resolves, the losing branch is **annulled, not scored**. Counterfactual worlds should be visibly *retired*, never silently deleted."

Map-generation/display takeaways: arrow-per-outcome + bar-per-conditional glyph; table or `IF YES`/`IF NO` buttons; **annul, don't delete** retired branches.

## 2J. The multiple-stage fallacy — bears directly on generated-chain evaluation (§2a, line 33)

> "**(a) The multiple-stage fallacy.** Decompose into six stages, multiply, and the result is almost certainly far too small — stage probabilities are correlated and people fail to condition on "everything upstream already happened" ([LW](https://www.lesswrong.com/w/multiple-stage-fallacy), [Kaufman](https://www.jefftk.com/p/multiple-stage-fallacy)). A tool that naively multiplies edge probabilities will demo a **3% answer** to "does Hormuz opening lower oil prices" and lose the room. Mitigations: cap depth; add a noisy-OR leak term for residual paths; anchor the terminal node to a base rate or market-implied level and present the chain as a **shift from that anchor**; **show the chain-derived and a direct holistic estimate side by side, surfacing disagreement rather than hiding it.**"

The popular read ([ACX](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here)) is that scaffolds are worth about a model generation and finance-adjacent questions are where AI does relatively *best*. > "**Base rate before narrative.** Elicit the reference class and its historical frequency in a *separate call that has not seen the scenario*, then adjust in a second call. Merging them invites representativeness: a vivid chain scores high because it is a good *story*."

Key operational detail: **two separate calls**, and the base-rate call must **not have seen the scenario**. No citation attached to this item (the supporting literature is representativeness/Kahneman, invoked by name only).

## 1C. Conditionals, never joints (§3, item 2, line 52)

> "**Elicit conditionals, never joints.** Ask for `P(B|A)` and `P(B|¬A)`; compute the rest. A five-step chain at 0.8 per step is 0.33, and the model will call it "very likely" if allowed."

Worked number: **0.8^5 = 0.33** for a five-step chain. Citation: Tversky & Kahneman 1983 (linked to the Wikipedia conjunction-fallacy page, not the paper).

## 2A. Metaculus — resolvable propositions, conditional pairs, annulment (§1, line 9–11)

> "**Metaculus** — an event is not a phrase, it is a *resolvable proposition*. A question is title + background + **resolution criteria** + fine print + dates, and the criteria are load-bearing: they *"should stand on its own as a set of self-contained instructions"* and supersede the background ([FAQ](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/)). Fine print is a deliberate readability valve; questions pass an [approval checklist](https://www.metaculus.com/help/question-checklist/) before going live, because an ambiguous criterion poisons every forecast attached to it."

> "The relevant primitive is the **Conditional Pair**: "if the Parent resolves Yes, how does the Child resolve?" and "if No?", asked together. In the feed each Parent outcome is an **arrow** and each conditional probability a **bar** — a two-branch fork glyph; in the forecasting UI it is a table, or `IF YES` / `IF NO` buttons opening distribution editors. It exists because *"two forecasters could have the same forecasts… while having very different mental models of their relationship"* ([announcement](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nQhmiKeYPvFaEZfWc/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions)). **The gap between branches *is* the causal claim** — the unit of value is P(B|A) − P(B|¬A), not P(B|A). One more detail worth copying: when the Parent resolves, the losing branch is **annulled, not scored**. Counterfactual worlds should be visibly *retired*, never silently deleted."

Map-generation/display takeaways: arrow-per-outcome + bar-per-conditional glyph; table or `IF YES`/`IF NO` buttons; **annul, don't delete** retired branches.

## 1A. The empirical framing (§3 preamble, lines 47)

> "The empirical picture: scaffolded, retrieval-augmented LLMs approach crowd-aggregate accuracy ([Halawi et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18563)), and LLM *ensembles* are statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd on small question sets ([Schoenegger et al., Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adp1528)) — but on a leakage-free, continuously-refreshed benchmark superforecasters still beat the best LLM by Brier 0.068 vs 0.119 ([ForecastBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19839)), several times the GPT-4→GPT-4o gap. The popular read ([ACX](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here)) is that scaffolds are worth about a model generation and finance-adjacent questions are where AI does relatively *best*. Encouraging — but the scaffold is doing the work, not the model."

Numbers with citations: Brier **0.068** (superforecasters) vs **0.119** (best LLM), ForecastBench (arXiv 2409.19839). Qualifier attached: "statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd **on small question sets**"; ForecastBench is "**leakage-free, continuously-refreshed**" — i.e. the author is explicitly weighting the leakage-free benchmark above the parity results.

## 1B. Base rate first, then adjust (§3, item 1, line 51)

> "**Base rate before narrative.** Elicit the reference class and its historical frequency in a *separate call that has not seen the scenario*, then adjust in a second call. Merging them invites representativeness: a vivid chain scores high because it is a good *story*."

Key operational detail: **two separate calls**, and the base-rate call must **not have seen the scenario**. No citation attached to this item (the supporting literature is representativeness/Kahneman, invoked by name only).

## 1C. Conditionals, never joints (§3, item 2, line 52)

> "**Elicit conditionals, never joints.** Ask for `P(B|A)` and `P(B|¬A)`; compute the rest. Humans and LLMs both violate the conjunction rule — a detailed conjunction is judged *more* likely than its own conjunct ([Tversky & Kahneman 1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunction_fallacy)). A five-step chain at 0.8 per step is 0.33, and the model will call it "very likely" if allowed."

Worked number: **0.8^5 = 0.33** for a five-step chain. Citation: Tversky & Kahneman 1983 (linked to the Wikipedia conjunction-fallacy page, not the paper).

## 1D. Small ensembles, k samples, geometric mean of odds, dispersion (§3, item 3, line 53)

> "**Sample k ≥ 5 times** across prompt variants and ideally two model families, then **aggregate by geometric mean of odds** ([summary](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/sMjcjnnpoAQCcedL2/when-pooling-forecasts-use-the-geometric-mean-of-odds)). **Keep the spread**: dispersion across independent elicitations is a defensible first-order estimate of that parameter's uncertainty, feeding §4 at zero extra cost."

Three separable claims: (a) **k ≥ 5**, varied over **prompt variants** and **ideally two model families**; (b) aggregate by **geometric mean of odds**; (c) **retain the dispersion** as the parameter's uncertainty.

Note on evidentiary status: the geometric-mean-of-odds link is an **EA Forum post** ("summary"), not a peer-reviewed source. **`k ≥ 5` carries no citation** — it is the author's judgement. This is a gap if the parent agent expected a median-vs-geomean-vs-arithmetic argument.

## 2A. Metaculus — resolvable propositions, conditional pairs, annulment (§1, line 9–11)

> "**Metaculus** — an event is not a phrase, it is a *resolvable proposition*. Fine print is a deliberate readability valve; questions pass an [approval checklist](https://www.metaculus.com/help/question-checklist/) before going live, because an ambiguous criterion poisons every forecast attached to it."

> "The relevant primitive is the **Conditional Pair**: "if the Parent resolves Yes, how does the Child resolve?" and "if No?", asked together. In the feed each Parent outcome is an **arrow** and each conditional probability a **bar** — a two-branch fork glyph; in the forecasting UI it is a table, or `IF YES` / `IF NO` buttons opening distribution editors. It exists because *"two forecasters could have the same forecasts… while having very different mental models of their relationship"* ([announcement](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nQhmiKeYPvFaEZfWc/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions)). **The gap between branches *is* the causal claim** — the unit of value is P(B|A) − P(B|¬A), not P(B|A). One more detail worth copying: when the Parent resolves, the losing branch is **annulled, not scored**. Counterfactual worlds should be visibly *retired*, never silently deleted."

Map-generation/display takeaways: arrow-per-outcome + bar-per-conditional glyph; table or `IF YES`/`IF NO` buttons; **annul, don't delete** retired branches.
